classification.difficultyReason: Apply exact ratios; the second part links two right triangles and requires solving an equation involving a surd.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC, with A above BC, a right-angle mark at A, and a 30-degree angle at C.
spec.mathematics: BC is the hypotenuse labelled square root of 8 cm; AB is labelled x cm.

spec.description: Linked right triangles share AD. B, C and D lie in order on a horizontal baseline; A is vertically above D. The dimension arrow spans BC only.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABD is 45 degrees, angle ACD is 60 degrees, angle ADC is a right angle, BC is 10 cm, and AD is x cm.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths or answers are visible.

answer.short:
$x=5(3+\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}$

Use the exact tangent ratios in the two right triangles and $BD=BC+CD$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABD$:

$$\begin{align*}\tan45^\circ&=\frac{x}{BD}\\BD&=x\end{align*}$$

In $\triangle ACD$:

$$\begin{align*}\tan60^\circ&=\frac{x}{CD}\\CD&=\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\end{align*}$$

Since $BD=BC+CD$:

$$\begin{align*}x&=10+\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\\\sqrt{3}x&=10\sqrt{3}+x\\(\sqrt{3}-1)x&=10\sqrt{3}\\x&=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-1}\\x&=\frac{10\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)}\\x&=\frac{30+10\sqrt{3}}{2}\\x&=5(3+\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
